title: Evidence-Weighted Trust Model for AI Formal Verification: Combining Compilation Rate, Vacuity Rate, and Human Review Time

original_idea.body:
# Evidence-Weighted Trust Model for AI Formal Verification: Combining Compilation Rate, Vacuity Rate, and Human Review Time

**Problem:** Safety decisions about deploying AI-generated formally verified code should weigh multiple evidence dimensions (compilation rate, vacuity rate, spec completeness, human review). No evidence-weighted trust model exists for this decision.

**Direction:** Propose and operationalize an evidence-weighted trust score for AI formal verification. Collect all five metrics (compilation rate, vacuity rate, mutation survival, human review time, spec completeness) on 30 VeriBench tasks. Fit a weighted model that predicts 'would an expert approve this for deployment?' Test model accuracy.

**Why it matters:** A principled trust score enables safety-conscious deployment decisions. Without it, organizations rely on single metrics (typically compilation rate) that are insufficient. This provides the formal methods analog of a structured safety case.

**Relevant context:** Safety cases in aerospace and medical devices combine multiple evidence sources. No analogous model exists for AI formal verification. This bridges safety case methodology from other engineering disciplines with the emerging formal verification AI field.
